h1: PS Mae Sod Hotel — a new-build hotel near Robinson Mae Sot with rooms cleaner than the price suggests
intro: In Mae Sot, where most places to stay are guesthouses and small lodges, the name that keeps coming up for anyone after a new-build hotel with a lift and clean rooms under THB 1,000 is PS Mae Sod Hotel · a budget hotel in a 7-storey building with around 79–80 rooms, located at 365 Moo 10, Mae Pa, near Robinson Mae Sot and Mae Sot Airport · what real reviews mention most often is that the rooms are clean, the building is new, parking is easy, and the starting price stays under THB 1,000 — which is hard to find for rooms in this condition · it suits people on border errands, travellers using Mae Sot as a stopover before heading on to Umphang, and anyone who wants a good-value bed without caring about a pool or fancy facilities · rooms start at about THB 500/night, scoring around 7.9 from real guest reviews.

body.html: Overview and who it suits — Mae Sot is the westernmost border town of Tak province, right next to Myawaddy in Myanmar, a busy trading town day and night. But when it comes to places to stay, most options are still guesthouses, small lodges and mid-sized local hotels · for anyone looking for a new-build hotel with a lift, clean rooms and a price under THB 1,000 without paying big-chain rates, the name that comes up most is PS Mae Sod Hotel, or as locals call it, PS Mae Sot · the hotel is a 7-storey building with around 79–80 rooms, set in Mae Pa on the side closer to Robinson Mae Sot and Mae Sot Airport · from reading real reviews across several platforms, the people it clearly suits are: those on border business or trade who need to stay a night in Mae Sot without paying much, budget travellers using Mae Sot as a stopover before catching onward transport to Umphang for Thi Lo Su Waterfall, couples or solo travellers who just want a clean room to sleep in, and people driving their own car who want somewhere with easy parking · on the flip side, if you're expecting a hotel with a pool, gym or a full-day resort feel, this may not match the picture, because its niche is an in-town budget hotel that prioritises value and cleanliness over a full facility list · to put it as plainly as possible, PS Mae Sod Hotel plays the "rooms better than the price" card well in a border-town context, which is why its overall score from real reviews sits at a satisfying 7.9 and why people come back, because they know exactly what they're getting.

Location and getting around — PS Mae Sod Hotel is located at 365 Moo 10, Mae Pa, Mae Sot, Tak, a zone that's not far from the town's main road and easy to get in and out of · the landmark locals use for directions is that the hotel is a short drive from Robinson Mae Sot, the biggest mall in town and a reference point everyone knows, which makes it easy to find and handy when you want food or shopping · a big plus of this location is that it's close to Mae Sot Airport (MAQ), only about 3 km away or under a 10 min drive, so anyone flying straight into Mae Sot who wants to reach their room quickly will be very comfortable · for Mae Sot's popular spots, the hotel has easy onward travel to the Mae Sot border, the Thai–Myanmar Friendship Bridge and Rim Moei Market, where you can cross to Myawaddy, all about a 10–15 min drive away · if you're planning to continue to Umphang for Thi Lo Su, be prepared for the Mae Sot–Umphang route to be a winding mountain road of about 150 km that takes several hours to drive, so staying one night in Mae Sot and setting off in the morning is the plan many people choose, and PS's location near the airport and the road out of town fits that plan nicely · one note on getting around: Mae Sot doesn't have as much public transport as bigger cities, so if you're not driving your own car, you should plan ahead for hire cars or ask the hotel in advance, because hailing a ride in Mae Sot at certain times can take longer than in major tourist towns.

"New building, clean room, really comfortable to sleep in for this price. There's parking too, and it's not far from Robinson, so it's easy to drive out for food. Great for coming to run errands and staying one night — genuinely better value than the price."

Rooms and decor — PS Mae Sod Hotel has around 79–80 rooms spread across a 7-storey building served by a lift, which is something a lot of people look for because many similarly priced places in Mae Sot are low-rise buildings with no lift · the main room types are Standard single, Standard twin and Deluxe, the last a little larger · the room style is plain and clean with a bright tone, focused on practical use rather than fancy decor · in-room facilities are a complete budget-hotel standard: air conditioning, flat-screen TV, fridge, work desk, hairdryer and an en-suite bathroom with a shower · the praise that comes up most in real reviews is that rooms are very clean, the building is new, the decor looks good, the bed is comfortable and it feels private, which many say is beyond expectations for a starting price under THB 1,000 · some reviews even say they got a room in better condition than pricier hotels in the same area · but to be straight, there are also some recurring notes, namely water pressure in some rooms that a few people say isn't very strong, and noise from outside or neighbouring rooms that you'll hear in some rooms, since it's an in-town hotel whose walls aren't soundproofed to luxury-hotel standard · overall, on the room front, PS Mae Sod does well and offers great value in its price bracket; the tip from reviews is that if quiet matters to you, try asking for a higher floor or a room away from the main road for a better night's sleep.

Facilities — let's be straight from the start: PS Mae Sod Hotel is an in-town budget hotel, not a resort, so there's no pool and no gym · anyone set on a place with a pool for the kids or a full day of lounging should look at other options in Mae Sot instead · but what PS does have, and does well for a hotel at this price, are the basic facilities you actually use every day · there's a lift in the 7-storey building, which makes hauling bags up to your room much easier, parking that many reviews praise as convenient and a reason drivers choose this place, free Wi-Fi in the common areas and rooms, a 24-hour front desk for those arriving late or leaving before dawn, and a restaurant and a meeting/multipurpose room on-site for group functions or small seminars · there are also basic services like a reception desk, luggage storage and common areas to sit and rest · the note on facilities found in reviews is that the Wi-Fi signal in some rooms or at some times can be less stable than it should be, so anyone who needs to work online seriously should have a mobile-data backup plan · overall, if you see this as a budget hotel that covers the essentials rather than one selling fancy facilities, PS does its job well and matches the price.

Food and breakfast — food is the point where information differs quite a bit between platforms. Some list breakfast as included in the room rate, while others list it as a restaurant where you order separately · what's clear is that the hotel has an on-site restaurant, and some reviews praise the food as tasty, which you don't often hear from a hotel at this price · on the notes side, though, some reviews say the breakfast has fairly few options, some items such as fried eggs may cost extra, and at busy times the seating and food may not be enough · the safest advice is to check the breakfast terms clearly when booking on each platform, whether it's included or not, because each room rate and promo period may differ · the upside of the location is that the hotel is near Robinson and Mae Sot's dining area, so a short drive out gets you to local restaurants, Burmese and Tai Yai eateries, coffee shops and budget-friendly food spots · many people choose to head out for meals rather than eat at the hotel every time, which is both cheaper and a chance to try the distinctive border-town food of Mae Sot, especially at Rim Moei Market and in town, where there's plenty to choose from.

Service — service is another area where PS Mae Sod Hotel earns fairly consistent praise in real reviews · many guests say the same thing: the staff are friendly, kind and helpful, whether with check-in and check-out, giving travel tips or sorting out various things · for a border town where there still aren't many people working in hospitality, the team's attentiveness is a point that makes the overall stay feel good and warm in a small-town-hotel way · there's a 24-hour front desk, which is very handy for anyone arriving late or needing to set off before dawn to catch a ride to Umphang or cross the border · but for balance, some reviews note that the welcome and the readiness of rooms isn't always consistent across the board — for example, some staff aren't fully trained on hospitality, and sometimes the room isn't ready at check-in time so you have to wait · these notes are normal for a budget hotel with a limited team, and overall service remains a clear plus and one reason the hotel's total score sits at a satisfying level.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling together Agoda, Trip.com and other review sources, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: new building and clean rooms is the most talked-about point, the room decor looks good and feels private, comfortable bed, friendly and helpful staff, convenient parking, tasty food, and great value compared with a starting price under THB 1,000 · many people agree it's a hotel offering rooms in better condition than the price in Mae Sot · on the notes side: the points raised are fairly few breakfast options with some items costing extra and seating and food possibly not being enough when busy, followed by water pressure in some rooms that isn't very strong, the Wi-Fi signal being unstable in some rooms or at some times, some staff still lacking hospitality training, and rooms sometimes not being ready at check-in so you have to wait · most of the gripes are small and manageable by setting the right expectations — seeing this as a budget hotel with clean rooms and good value in a border town, not a hotel selling a complete facility list or five-star service.

"Room was really clean, staff were lovely, parking was easy · the only small gripes were that the water in the room didn't flow very strongly and the breakfast had a few too few options. But for this price in Mae Sot, it's great value. Coming back next time for sure."

Price comparison and value — PS Mae Sod Hotel's room rates start at around THB 500/night for a Standard single at the regular rate, rising to about THB 600–650 for a Standard twin and about THB 750–900 for a Deluxe, with prices shifting by season and promotion · compared with other places in Mae Sot, which are mostly guesthouses or small hotels in a similar price range, PS's clear advantage is that it's a new building with a lift, clean rooms and the feel of a real hotel rather than a converted lodge, at a price that's still under THB 1,000 · for people on border errands, budget travellers or anyone using Mae Sot as a stopover before continuing to Umphang, this price for a room in good condition is great value · those who want a pool, gym or resort feel may need to bump the budget up to one of Mae Sot's big chains like Centara Life, which offers a fuller facility list but costs several times more · the safest advice is to compare prices directly across Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking, since each platform often has different promos and prices at different times, check clearly whether the price you see includes breakfast, and pick a free-cancellation option if your plans aren't firm yet.

Good to know before booking — there are several things that help make the stay smoother, gathered from reading real reviews · one, check the breakfast terms clearly, whether the room rate you book includes it or not, because the information differs by platform and some items may cost extra · two, if quiet and a good night's sleep matter, try asking for a higher floor or a room away from the main road at booking or check-in, since it's an in-town hotel where you may hear some noise from outside · three, if you have to work online seriously, keep a mobile-data backup plan, because the Wi-Fi in some rooms or at some times can be unstable · four, if you're driving, the hotel has parking, which is a strength, but ask about the number of spaces in advance during busy periods · five, plan on a simple breakfast at the hotel and then head out for other meals in Mae Sot town or at Rim Moei Market, so you can try the border-town food and save money · six, if you're planning to continue to Umphang for Thi Lo Su, allow time to set off in the morning because the route is a winding mountain road that takes several hours · seven, note the check-in time of 2:00 PM and check-out at 12:00 PM, and be prepared for the room to possibly not be ready at certain times — if you arrive early you may have to wait a little.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, PS Mae Sod Hotel is the best fit for anyone who wants a clean room in a new building, with a lift and easy parking, at a price under THB 1,000 in central Mae Sot · its clear strengths are room cleanliness, the newness of the building, friendly service and value that's hard to find in the same price bracket, making it a great fit for people on border business and trade, budget travellers, and anyone using Mae Sot as a stopover before Umphang or crossing the border · what you have to accept and set expectations for is that there's no pool or gym, the breakfast has few options, water pressure in some rooms isn't very strong, and the Wi-Fi is unstable at times · if you're after a hotel with a pool and a full facility list, this may not be the answer, and you should consider one of Mae Sot's big chains instead · but if you look at it in the Mae Sot context — a place with clean rooms, a new building, good value and reliable basics — PS Mae Sod Hotel does its job well and is one of the best-value options for an overnight stay in this border town.

faq.q: What's the starting price at PS Mae Sod Hotel · what rooms are there?

faq.q: Who does PS Mae Sod Hotel suit best?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people on border business and trade, budget travellers, and anyone using Mae Sot as a stopover before Umphang or crossing the border who want a clean room in a new building, with a lift and easy parking, at a price under THB 1,000 · if you want a pool or gym, one of Mae Sot's big chains may suit you better.

faq.q: Does PS Mae Sod Hotel have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: There's no pool and no gym, as it's an in-town budget hotel focused on clean rooms and value · breakfast is available, but the information differs by platform on whether it's included in the room rate, and the options are fairly few with some items possibly costing extra, so check the terms clearly when booking.

faq.q: Are PS Mae Sod Hotel's review scores trustworthy?
faq.a: PS Mae Sod Hotel is a building with around 79–80 rooms, and the overall score from real reviews sits at about 7.9, with Agoda around 7.8–8.2 from over 100 reviews · its strengths are room cleanliness, the newness of the building, and value at a price under THB 1,000, ideal if you want a clean place for an overnight stay in Mae Sot without focusing on fancy facilities.
